headline: Highest risk is cascading error: OpenMetadata can consume Dagster-produced metadata and act on it via MCP/APIs, creating default-path trust and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem write, or MCP surfaces, so direct injection into it is blocked. OpenMetadata can ingest external content through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, so if Dagster outputs are manually bridged into those channels, prompt-like content could be misread. This is a limited, non-default pathway.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are manually copied into OpenMetadata MCP/API inputs, then instruction-like text can be interpreted as data.
IF an operator routes Dagster-generated text through a shared channel, then injection risk becomes active.
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between the tools.
Use a strict schema for any Dagster-to-OpenMetadata payloads.
Strip free-form text before sending to OpenMetadata.
Review MCP tool inputs for instruction-like strings before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes in the profile and has no filesystem or network egress, while OpenMetadata touches technical metadata, lineage, governance, and memory/tribal knowledge and can send data through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If Dagster jobs feed metadata into OpenMetadata, sensitive operational context can be exposed in default workflows. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Dagster job metadata includes secrets, identifiers, or internal notes and is forwarded to OpenMetadata, then leakage occurs.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs are configured to export catalog content externally, then stored metadata can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Redact secrets from Dagster metadata before export.
Limit OpenMetadata ingestion to approved metadata fields.
Turn off outbound webhooks unless required.
Audit API payloads for sensitive fields.
Use separate service accounts for each system.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable local resources with OpenMetadata in the profile. OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and uses MCP/APIs rather than local writes here. Any conflict would require an external shared resource not shown, so the pathway is weak and unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable API resource, then write contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds a shared writable workspace not shown in either profile, then conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared APIs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, and OpenMetadata exposes APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP, so Dagster-produced metadata can become authoritative input for OpenMetadata workflows. If OpenMetadata acts on Dagster output without verification, errors can cascade into catalog, lineage, or governance records. The default-path trust chain is dangerous and can propagate incorrect facts broadly.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Dagster output without validation, then incorrect lineage or governance records can be created.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP tools trigger downstream actions from Dagster-derived metadata, then errors cascade.
mitigations: Add validation between Dagster and OpenMetadata.
Require human review for lineage changes.
Reject malformed or incomplete metadata.
Log and diff incoming records before commit.
Disable auto-triggered webhooks for untrusted inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster has no touched data classes listed, while OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include regulated or internal data. OpenMetadata also uses APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, creating residency and retention exposure if those records are exported or logged. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated metadata is stored in OpenMetadata and exported through APIs or webhooks, then retention/residency controls must apply.
IF Dagster pipelines annotate records with personal or internal governance data, then compliance obligations attach.
mitigations: Classify metadata before ingestion.
Set retention limits on OpenMetadata records.
Disable exports for regulated fields.
Document data residency for API/webhook destinations.
Review deletion/export workflows.
